newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman sets deadline for business to employ Omanis.
newsitem.headline: Oman sets deadline for business to employ Omanis.

text.p: Oman has given private sector businesses until the end of 1997 to detail plans on how to employ more nationals in an active drive to "Omanise" its workforce, officials said.
The Labour and Social Development Ministry asked transport and storage companies to submit plans on how to "Omanise more than 60 percent" of their workforce by end-1998, they added.
It asked banks, insurance firms and real estate agencies to detail how they planned to make sure at least 45 percent of their employees were nationals, they added.
It set 35 percent, 30 percent and 20 percent targets for the share of local citizens in the workforce of industries, restaurants and hotels, and wholesale traders respectively.

According to ministry figures, 351,619 foreign workers, mostly Asians, were employed in the private sector in 1995 along with 25,087 Omanis. Of the total 110,444 employed by the public sector in 1995, 44,767 were foreigners.
All Gulf Arab states have begun a drive to find more jobs for their citizens and reduce their reliance on expatriates.
A Gulf official said in December that foreign workers accounted for more than 80 percent, and in some cases 90 percent, of labourers in some Gulf states.
